newsitem.title: USA: Sequus sees Q1 revs lower than Q4.
newsitem.headline: Sequus sees Q1 revs lower than Q4.

text.p: Sequus Pharmaceuticals Inc said it expects first quarter revenues to be between $8 and $8.5 million, below the 1996 fourth quarter's, including payments from Schering-Plough Corp .
The company entered an agreement in September for Schering to market its Caelyx anti-cancer drug. It did not say how much the Schering deal contributed to sales.
The first quarter sales forecast compares with sales of $9,259,000 in last year's fourth quarter and $4,457,000 in the year-ago first quarter.

Sequus said the decrease in revenues from the fourth quarter is due mainly to reduced product sales in the U.S. It also said operating expenses will be down from the fourth quarter, mainly as a result of lower selling, general and administrative expenses.

"The primary issue in the first quarter appears to be a longer than anticipated hospital formulary decision process for Amphotec," Dr. I. Craig Henderson, Sequus chairman and chief executive officer said in a statement. "We are encouraged by the decisions of a number of major hospitals to use Amphotec; however, the timing of these decisions and the actual product purchases are somewhat later than expected."
He also said that the use of protease inhibitors in AIDS patients had reduced the incidence of Kaposi's sarcoma and the demand for its Doxil drug for use in patients with solid tumors.
